summary: This bill increases certain VA disability compensation payments by adding a $833.33 monthly supplemental allowance for aid-and-attendance recipients, ties future dependency and indemnity compensation rates to Social Security increases plus extra percentages for two cycles starting December 2026, extends housing loan fee tables and pension payment limits through September 2036, and expands VA home loan eligibility to National Guard and reserve members with at least 14 days of qualifying service after entry-level training (retroactive to September 2001) subject to an added 1% loan fee.

scores.thoughts: The bill directly increases monthly disability compensation payments (new supplemental allowance of $833.33), raises dependency and indemnity compensation rates above Social Security COLAs for two cycles, extends pension payment limits, and expands VA home-loan eligibility to additional Guard/Reserve members. All of these changes increase federal outlays for veterans' benefits.
The bill contains no provisions altering tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue measures.
The legislation adjusts disability compensation and home-loan fees administered by the VA but does not change coverage rules, provider networks, or the structure of VA healthcare delivery itself.
No provisions address firearms, background checks, or gun regulations.
No immigration, visa, or border-related language appears in the bill.
The bill is silent on reproductive health services or abortion access.
While the bill benefits veterans of military service, it does not authorize or alter funding for active-duty forces, weapons systems, or Department of Defense operations.
No environmental, energy, or regulatory provisions are present.
The core purpose is to expand cash benefits (disability compensation, DIC, pensions) and housing assistance for veterans, directly enlarging a federal safety-net program.
No education funding, school-choice, or student-aid provisions exist.
The bill does not address controlled substances, decriminalization, or enforcement.
No sentencing, policing, or criminal-justice reform language is included.
The legislation contains no trade, tariff, or globalization measures.
By increasing mandatory spending on veterans' benefits without offsetting revenue, the bill adds to future deficits.
No provisions expand or restrict legal protections on the basis of sexual orientation or gender identity.
The bill does not address foreign assistance programs.
No election-administration or voting-access provisions are present.
The legislation is silent on data privacy, technology regulation, or surveillance.
No labor, union, or workplace-rights language appears.
The bill does not address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
